user.title: Live Heating Costs
user.description: Set up the hub that all heat sources will share: the live buy price, optional day-ahead/forecast price sensors, and the house's outdoor-temperature and demand model. Heat sources (wood stove, resistive element, heat pump, …) are added afterwards from the integration's page.

data_description.buy_price_entity: Your all-in live electricity buy price in EUR/kWh (e.g. sensor.nordpool_total_buying_cost). Used to compute the live cost of every heat source right now.
data_description.day_ahead_entity: A sensor exposing today/tomorrow price slots in its attributes (e.g. Nord Pool, ENTSO-e, or a day-ahead template). Used to show the cost trend for the next slots.
data_description.forecast_price_entity: A predictor sensor estimating prices beyond the real day-ahead horizon. Used only for slots later than the known prices.
data_description.weather_entity: A weather entity whose forecast can stand in for the outdoor-temperature sensor when it's briefly unavailable.
data_description.outdoor_temp_entity: The outdoor-temperature sensor used to look up heat-pump COP/capacity and to drive the internal heat-demand model.
data_description.demand_mode: How much heat the house needs right now: measured from an existing sensor, or estimated from outdoor temperature with a heat-loss model.

demand.title: Heat demand
demand.description: Configure how live heat demand (kW) is determined.

data.ua_learning: Learn UA from measured heating history

data_description.demand_entity: A sensor that already reports how much heat the house needs (kW or kWh/day).
data_description.demand_unit: Whether the demand sensor reports instantaneous power (kW) or a daily energy total (kWh/day).
data_description.base_temp: The outdoor temperature above which the house needs no heating (its 'balance point'). Demand is modelled as UA × max(0, base_temp − outdoor_temp).
data_description.ua_seed_w_per_c: House heat-loss coefficient. 140 W/°C reproduces the legacy heating-demand constant; it will be refined automatically when learning is on.
data_description.ua_learning: When on, the seed UA above is continuously refined from measured delivered heat vs. outdoor temperature, so the model improves over time instead of staying fixed at the seed.
data_description.backfill_days: How many days of history to replay on first start to warm up the UA learner immediately, instead of waiting for that many days of live data.

error.buy_price_not_numeric: That sensor's state isn't a plain number (EUR/kWh). Point this at a live buy-price sensor.
error.invalid_price_format: That sensor doesn't expose a recognised price forecast (no today/tomorrow price list found in its attributes).

abort.already_configured: This buy-price sensor is already configured.

init.title: Add a heat source
init.description: Name the source and pick how it's modelled. The type can't be changed later — delete and re-add the source to switch types.

data_description.source_type: Curve = a heat pump with a measured/published COP(T) and capacity(T) table. Dynamic, fixed COP = an electric source whose efficiency doesn't depend on temperature (resistive heating = COP 1.0). Fixed-cost fuel = wood or another fuel priced per unit, independent of the live electricity price.

static.title: Fixed-cost fuel source
static.description: A fuel-derived heat source (e.g. a wood stove) priced independently of the live electricity price. Capacity 0 means the source contributes heat (and is used for UA learning) but is never dispatched/controlled — useful for a wood sauna whose heat reaches the house only via heat-recovery ventilation. Event mode suits exactly that: a fixed kWh is credited each time the sauna switches on, debounced so a single burn isn't counted twice.

data_description.fuel_unit: The unit the price is quoted per: cubic metres of stacked wood, kilograms, or kWh directly.
data_description.price_per_unit_eur: What you pay per unit of fuel, in euro.
data_description.energy_density_kwh_per_unit: Energy content of one unit of fuel. Suggested default is 1700 kWh/m³ for stacked birch — adjust for your wood/fuel and unit.
data_description.efficiency: Fraction of the fuel's energy that ends up as delivered heat (stove + flue losses).
data_description.capacity_kw: Maximum heat output. Set to 0 for a source that contributes heat but is never dispatched (e.g. a wood sauna) — it's still counted for cost/UA learning.
data_description.activity_mode: None = no on/off detection (a constant background contributor). Duration = integrate a known output while the activity sensor is on. Event = credit a fixed amount of energy each time the activity sensor switches on, useful for a sauna heated in distinct sessions.
data_description.activity_entity: The switch/binary_sensor/input_boolean that reports when this source is actively producing heat.
data_description.active_output_kw: Assumed heat output while the activity sensor is on (duration mode).
data_description.energy_per_event_kwh: Fixed heat delivered per activation, e.g. one sauna heating session (event mode).
data_description.event_debounce_hours: Minimum gap between two activations for them to count as separate events, so a single long burn with brief interruptions isn't double-counted.

dynamic_fixed.title: Electric, fixed COP
dynamic_fixed.description: An electric heat source whose efficiency doesn't vary with outdoor temperature — resistive heating (COP 1.0) or any electric source with a known constant COP.

data_description.cop: Heat output ÷ electricity input, assumed constant regardless of outdoor temperature. Use 1.0 for pure resistive heating.
data_description.energy_entity: Cumulative kWh counter metering this source. When set, its consumption feeds the heating-demand learner (delivered heat = energy × COP).

curve_entities.title: Heat pump (COP curve) — sensors
curve_entities.description: The live sensors this heat pump reports. COP/capacity tables are configured on the next step.

data_description.power_entity: The pump's live electrical power draw (W). Used to detect when it's actively heating.
data_description.energy_entity: A cumulative (total_increasing) energy counter (kWh) for the pump, used to compute delivered heat via COP over a window.
data_description.climate_entity: Optional climate entity whose hvac_action gates 'heating' state, tightening when the COP/capacity tables apply.
data_description.pump_temp_entity: If the pump reports its own outdoor-temperature reading, prefer it over the hub's outdoor-temperature sensor for this source's COP lookup.
data_description.temp_entity_override: Use a different outdoor-temperature sensor for just this source instead of the hub's.
data_description.standby_w: Power below which the pump is considered idle (not heating), rather than running at very low output.
data_description.blend_window_min: Window used to smooth the live power/energy signal into a stable COP estimate.

curve_tables.title: Heat pump (COP curve) — tables
curve_tables.description: Pick a built-in pump preset, or choose 'Custom' and paste your own COP(T) and capacity(T) tables as 'temp:value' pairs (e.g. '-30:1.35, -25:1.6, 7:4.2') or a JSON list of [temp, value] pairs. Changing the preset dropdown refreshes the tables below with that preset's values instead of saving immediately — submit again to confirm.

data_description.preset: A built-in measured/published table for a known pump, or 'Custom' to enter your own.
data_description.cop_points: COP at each outdoor temperature, interpolated linearly between points and clamped flat beyond the endpoints. Ignored (and replaced) unless the preset is 'Custom'.
data_description.capacity_points: Maximum heat output (kW) at each outdoor temperature, same format as the COP table. Ignored (and replaced) unless the preset is 'Custom'.
data_description.operating_limit_c: Below this outdoor temperature the pump can't operate at all.
data_description.min_cop: Sanity floor: a computed COP below this is treated as implausible/unavailable rather than reported.
data_description.max_cop: Sanity ceiling: a computed COP above this is treated as implausible/unavailable rather than reported.

error.invalid_curve_format: Couldn't parse that table. Use 'temp:value' pairs separated by commas or newlines (e.g. '-30:1.35, 7:4.2'), or a JSON list of [temp, value] pairs.
error.invalid_curve_points: That table isn't valid: it needs at least 2 points, no duplicate temperatures, and all values greater than 0.

log_wood.name: Log wood heat
log_wood.description: Manually log delivered heat from a wood/fuel source, either as a direct kWh figure or as a fuel-unit count (converted using the source's configured energy density and efficiency). Specify exactly one of energy_kwh or units.

units.name: Fuel units
units.description: Fuel quantity consumed, in the source's configured fuel unit (m³, kg or kWh).

source.name: Source
source.description: Title or subentry ID of the static (wood) source to log against. Defaults to the first configured static source.
